newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says not yet known if Arafat was target.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says not yet known if Arafat was target.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday it had not yet determined whether two detainees had planned to kill Palestinian President Yasser Arafat during an Islamic summit conference in Islamabad last month.

The statement by Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan in the Senate (upper house of parliament) came a day after Arafat was quoted by the official Palestinian news agency WAFA as saying that Pakistani authorities had detained suspects who were plotting to kill him during his Islamabad visit.
Gohar, quoted by Pakistan's official APP news agency, said the government was interrogating the two suspects arrested by its intelligence agencies.
He said the matter was being investigated and "there has been no identification as yet who the target was". He did not identify the suspects or give their nationality.

Pakistani police killed six Moslem radicals -- four Arabs and two Tajiks -- at an Afghan refugee camp near the northwestern town of Peshawar on March 27 after a five-day standoff that began on the day of the Islamic summit, March 23.
Some police officials say the dead radicals of the so-called Takfiri group may have planned to disturb the Islamabad summit, but they have no definite information.
Interior Minister Shujaat Hussain told the Senate on Thursday he would submit a detailed report about the incident in a couple of days.
